taxonomy.title: Skin — melanoma and cutaneous cancer
taxonomy.scopeIn: Melanoma biopsy/microstaging, excision, nodal staging and systemic-treatment principles, plus BCC, cSCC and Merkel carcinoma.
taxonomy.scopeOut: Soft-tissue sarcoma/desmoid belongs to soft-tissue-sarcoma-desmoid. Breast Paget belongs to breast-cancer. General cancer genetics belongs to oncology-genetics-principles.
taxonomy.priorityReason: Depth, risk and tissue adequacy provide important surgery and staging decisions.
taxonomy.coverageReason: Live identities cover part of this scope. The research agenda flags breadth to check, and the topic worker must judge redundancy and question quality.
taxonomy.testingWeightBasis: Owner-directed editorial estimate of general-surgery testing relevance. No exam percentages or official blueprint weights are asserted.

concepts.displayName: Recognize a basal cell carcinoma pattern
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize clinical patterns concerning for BCC and arrange diagnostic confirmation.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Counsel about BCC disease behavior
concepts.learningObjective: Explain that local destruction is the principal concern and metastasis is rare without minimizing advanced disease.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Diagnostic biopsy of a suspicious keratinocyte lesion
concepts.learningObjective: Select adequate diagnostic biopsy for a suspicious lesion before cSCC risk-directed treatment.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Risk-directed surgery for cutaneous SCC
concepts.learningObjective: Choose standard excision for low-risk cSCC and Mohs-capable referral for high-risk cSCC.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Attribute bowel melanoma to its confirmed skin primary
concepts.learningObjective: Use a supplied cutaneous primary and confirmatory outside pathology to identify small-bowel melanoma as metastatic disease retaining the primary cancer's identity.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Merkel sentinel-node staging
concepts.learningObjective: Refer an appropriate clinically node-negative Merkel cell carcinoma candidate for sentinel-node staging rather than equating a normal node examination with pathologic node negativity.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Cutaneous neuroendocrine carcinoma recognition
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize Merkel cell carcinoma from an integrated cutaneous neuroendocrine pathology assessment rather than assuming every skin nodule is squamous cancer.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Sentinel-node staging discussion for melanoma
concepts.learningObjective: Discuss sentinel lymph-node biopsy for pathological regional staging of intermediate-thickness clinically node-negative melanoma alongside definitive excision planning.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Apply regional-node evidence before sentinel staging
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a clinically node-negative melanoma basin from a proven-positive or suspicious nonrepresentatively sampled node, and choose the appropriate next diagnostic/staging pathway.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Skin-cancer risk beyond size
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate adverse tissue features with lesion size before choosing a low-risk skin-cancer operation.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Complete diagnostic biopsy of a suspicious pigmented lesion
concepts.learningObjective: Select complete diagnostic excision with narrow margins and adequate depth for a small accessible pigmented lesion concerning for melanoma.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Resolve partial skin-biopsy and microstaging limitations
concepts.learningObjective: Choose a representative diagnostic completion strategy when specimen location, deep transection or clinicopathologic discordance prevents a reliable whole-lesion diagnosis or microstage before definitive reconstruction/staging.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Interpret mapped partial specimens before melanoma planning
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate the specimen's location, represented tissue compartments and cut surface to retain valid local findings while limiting whole-lesion diagnosis or depth claims before completion pathology.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Select diagnostic extent after a locally in-situ partial specimen
concepts.learningObjective: Apply an adequately described local epidermal melanoma finding to the next primary-site procedure without extending that finding to an unrepresented raised residual component.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Complete sampling of a changing residual pigmented lesion
concepts.learningObjective: Choose complete diagnostic sampling after a benign limited sector fails to represent a changing residual lesion at a site suitable for excision.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

concepts.displayName: Integrate partial depth records before a nodal-staging discussion
concepts.learningObjective: Preserve demonstrated invasive depth across mapped partial specimens and decide whether that evidence already supports a sentinel-node staging discussion while primary assessment continues.
concepts.assignmentBasis: Organ/decision-family assignment reviewed against the topic scope.

recordedHolds.reason: The staging decision is resolved before incision in this scenario. Creating a current operative change would require a new directly verified finding and sequence; a preoperative rule disguised as an intra-op consult is not emitted.

decision.title: Choose a representative diagnostic specimen from the map

cues.phrase: the fragment diagnosis is not relabelled
cues.why: This unnecessary caption tells the learner to retain the benign fragment diagnosis rather than reconsider it. It weakly coaches evidence interpretation, but does not choose between complete excision and a targeted deep punch; both respect that diagnosis.

fairness: Original flag resolved: YES at the objective level for the mapped importance concern; no separate in-game flag is recorded. Owner b1-B12-context note fully resolved: YES. Choosing a representative next diagnostic specimen for an interval-changing residual lesion is a practical decision, rather than debating a report/request label.

Moderate at the lower end for PGY-2/3. First recognize that the valid benign lateral fragment does not establish the nature of the new unsampled medial focus; then choose complete diagnostic sampling over a second focal sample or observation. The targeted medial deep punch is a materially closer competitor than the prior wrong-block or superficial-biopsy foils.

Narrow-margin excision is the best offered diagnostic approach for the described small discrete residual upper-arm patch. The specimen map and interval change establish why the existing benign sample cannot settle the whole-lesion question. A side-edge melanocytic proliferation alone should not be taught as an automatic malignancy or excision indication.

A deep targeted punch is not inherently invalid and can be appropriate when complete sampling is unsuitable. The supplied small discrete patch and ordinary upper-arm site support the ranking here without the prohibited closure-feasibility assurance. The review does not infer an exact lesion diameter, closure technique or universal excision rule.

No equally strong offered key or confident clinical inaccuracy identified in this particular setting. 'Narrow-margin' should remain a diagnostic procedure, not an implied definitive melanoma excision or invented margin width. Clinician confirmation of the intended depth/completeness remains necessary.

The former classic-color and closure-permission cues are removed. Both biopsy options address the newly described medial area, and two options repeat 'residual patch', so simple location/phrase matching does not uniquely select the key.
suggestions: Trim the caption to 'Specimen and interval record'; the fragment-diagnosis commentary is unnecessary even though it does not reveal the complete key.

Retain the mapped sample location, interval change and credible targeted-biopsy alternative. Keep the explanation explicit that the old fragment may be correctly diagnosed while the residual lesion is not fully assessed.
Have clinical sign-off confirm that the excision label communicates complete diagnostic sampling at appropriate depth without adding an unsupported numerical margin or a feasibility sentence.

approvedQuestion.stem: Which diagnosis is best supported by this skin biopsy?

answerChoices.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
answerChoices.rationale: Integrates skin location, morphology and the panel; no single stain alone establishes the diagnosis.

answerChoices.label: Metastatic pulmonary small-cell carcinoma
answerChoices.rationale: Shares small-cell neuroendocrine morphology, making the pattern across CK20 and TTF1 important rather than the word small-cell alone.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Shares small-cell neuroendocrine morphology, making the pattern across CK20 and TTF1 important rather than the word small-cell alone.

answerChoices.label: Primary cutaneous malignant melanoma
answerChoices.rationale: A malignant skin nodule remains plausible initially, but the combined epithelial/neuroendocrine staining favors another lineage.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A malignant skin nodule remains plausible initially, but the combined epithelial/neuroendocrine staining favors another lineage.

answerChoices.label: Primary cutaneous malignant lymphoma
answerChoices.rationale: Small dermal malignant cells can suggest a lymphoid process before the integrated immunophenotype is considered.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Small dermal malignant cells can suggest a lymphoid process before the integrated immunophenotype is considered.

approvedQuestion.explanation: The morphology and combined CK20, synaptophysin and TTF1 pattern favor Merkel cell carcinoma among these options. Staining patterns have exceptions; no single marker definitively excludes pulmonary small-cell carcinoma or establishes Merkel cell carcinoma. Integrate the panel with the clinical and pathologic assessment.

question.stem: Which lesion category best fits the pattern?

question.explanation: Sentinel-node biopsy evaluates occult regional disease in an appropriate clinically node-negative patient. Do not apply a primary-thickness rule before establishing which basin category actually exists.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: Two mapped outside specimens are available. The earlier full-thickness punch from one sector contains invasive melanoma measuring 1.8 mm from the granular layer to the deepest tumor; that fragment's deep edge is free of tumor. A later shave from another sector measures 0.6 mm to melanoma at its deep cut surface. A firm focus remains in the residual lesion. No regional node is palpable at this visit. Completion sampling is being arranged.
decisionNodes.stem: Which provisional depth and nodal-discussion entry should accompany {patientName}'s completion-sampling request?

answerChoices.label: At least 1.8 mm; nodal-staging discussion supported
answerChoices.rationale: The greatest demonstrated invasive extent is not erased by a later shallower transected fragment. Even though the whole-lesion maximum is not final, the established depth is already in the range supporting a sentinel-node discussion in this clinically node-negative setting.

answerChoices.label: At least 0.6 mm; nodal-staging discussion supported
answerChoices.rationale: The general discussion direction does not repair the depth record: this drops the greater demonstrated invasive extent simply because another specimen was later or transected.

answerChoices.label: At least 1.8 mm; nodal-staging discussion deferred
answerChoices.rationale: This preserves the demonstrated extent but treats uncertainty about a possibly greater maximum as a reason to ignore a discussion boundary already crossed by known evidence.

answerChoices.label: At least 0.6 mm; nodal-staging discussion deferred
answerChoices.rationale: This both replaces the greater demonstrated extent with a later smaller value and uses incomplete maximum-depth assessment to defer an already supported discussion.

decisionNodes.explanation: Integrate the mapped specimens rather than replace one with the latest report. The 1.8-mm invasive measurement remains demonstrated; a 0.6-mm tumor-positive cut base cannot lower it. The whole-lesion maximum may still increase. The existing greater-than-1-mm guidance supports discussing sentinel-node staging in this clinically node-negative setting while primary assessment continues. It does not order a nodal procedure or determine how a later abnormal node should be assessed.

decisionNodes.stem: Which primary-site procedure should be arranged next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Excisional biopsy of the complete lesion
answerChoices.rationale: The sampled sector is epidermis confined, but its report does not establish the invasive status of the raised residual component. Complete diagnostic removal is feasible and can supply the architecture and maximum invasion information needed before selecting treatment extent.

answerChoices.label: Wide local excision for melanoma in situ
answerChoices.rationale: This converts a valid local epidermal diagnosis into a whole-lesion treatment classification before the raised residual focus is represented. A therapeutic plan based on that extension may use the wrong disease extent.

answerChoices.label: Full-thickness incisional biopsy of the raised focus
answerChoices.rationale: Targeting the raised component is a credible way to seek invasion information, but it again samples part of a lesion whose complete diagnostic removal is feasible, leaving whole-lesion architecture and maximum depth less fully represented.

decisionNodes.explanation: The represented dermis is explicitly free of the atypical melanoma cells, so the local epidermal diagnosis is supported. That does not classify a separate residual focus. When the whole suspicious lesion can be removed diagnostically, representative architecture and invasion assessment should precede selecting its treatment extent.

decisionNodes.stem: Which assessment should accompany {patientName}'s request for residual-lesion excision?

answerChoices.label: Melanocytic atypia shown; residual-lesion invasion unassessed
answerChoices.rationale: The sampled sector demonstrates a melanocytic abnormality, but that sector and tissue depth do not represent the separate residual raised focus. Retain the positive local finding without assigning a whole-lesion invasive status.

answerChoices.label: Melanocytic atypia shown; residual-lesion invasion excluded
answerChoices.rationale: The positive junctional finding is retained correctly, but the unsampled focus cannot be cleared of invasion by the peripheral fragment.

answerChoices.label: Melanocytic atypia unconfirmed; residual-lesion invasion unassessed
answerChoices.rationale: Sampling limits do not erase the actual cytologic/architectural abnormality in the submitted sector. This discards valid evidence while correctly withholding the whole-lesion conclusion.

answerChoices.label: Melanocytic atypia unconfirmed; residual-lesion invasion excluded
answerChoices.rationale: This discards the demonstrated abnormality and extends the fragment's limitations into an unsupported statement about the residual lesion.

decisionNodes.explanation: Map the reported abnormal junctional population to the sector actually sampled. It is valid evidence of atypia there, not a whole-lesion microstage. The separate raised residual focus remains unassessed for invasion. Completion pathology is needed for subsequent lesion-wide planning; a limited specimen is neither wholly useless nor a basis for clearing unrepresented tissue.

Completion pathology is needed for subsequent lesion-wide planning; a limited specimen is neither wholly useless nor a basis for clearing unrepresented tissue.

question.stem: Which diagnosis is best supported by the skin-biopsy morphology and combined staining pattern?

answerChoices.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
answerChoices.rationale: Integrates skin location, morphology and the panel; no single stain alone establishes the diagnosis.

answerChoices.label: Metastatic pulmonary small-cell carcinoma
answerChoices.rationale: Shares small-cell neuroendocrine morphology, making the pattern across CK20 and TTF1 important rather than the word small-cell alone.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Shares small-cell neuroendocrine morphology, making the pattern across CK20 and TTF1 important rather than the word small-cell alone.

answerChoices.label: Primary cutaneous malignant melanoma

question.stem: Which primary-site procedure is the best next plan for {patientName}?

exhibit.caption: Original constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Biopsy
items.value: Well-differentiated invasive squamous nests; measured depth 1.1 mm in the represented tissue.

items.label: Additional microscopic description
items.value: A tumor nest lies within the perineurium surrounding a small dermal nerve; tumor reaches a lateral biopsy edge.

items.label: Examination
items.value: Small residual lesion at the biopsy site; facial movement and light-touch sensation symmetric. Regional nodes not palpable.

answerChoices.label: Mohs micrographic surgery
answerChoices.rationale: The nerve-related microscopic finding represents perineural invasion, a high-risk feature despite the small diameter and otherwise favorable differentiation. It changes the margin-management pathway toward Mohs evaluation/treatment.

answerChoices.label: Elliptical excision with margin histology
answerChoices.rationale: This would fit the otherwise favorable superficial primary, but it underweights the nerve involvement that changes the represented risk-directed plan.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This would fit the otherwise favorable superficial primary, but it underweights the nerve involvement that changes the represented risk-directed plan.

answerChoices.label: Curettage and electrodesiccation
answerChoices.rationale: This treats the lesion as a selected superficial local lesion despite invasive tumor at a biopsy edge and the nerve involvement requiring margin-directed care.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: This treats the lesion as a selected superficial local lesion despite invasive tumor at a biopsy edge and the nerve involvement requiring margin-directed care.

question.explanation: The microscopic description, rather than an adverse-risk label, identifies perineural invasion. Small diameter, well-differentiated morphology and absence of sensory symptoms do not remove that recorded finding. High-risk cutaneous SCC should be evaluated for Mohs micrographic surgery. This primary-site question does not claim Mohs exhausts any additional neurological or staging evaluation, or that every standard-excision strategy is impossible.

exhibit.caption: Original constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations

items.label: Mapped primary-site specimens
items.value: An earlier peripheral fragment showed invasion to 0.5 mm. A subsequent representative central specimen showed a valid invasive depth of 1.4 mm; the reports map both to the same primary lesion.

items.label: Regional assessment
items.value: No palpable axillary node; ultrasound shows preserved nodal morphology.

items.label: Current field
items.value: The flap has been designed but has not been elevated across the surrounding skin.

answerChoices.label: Sentinel-node biopsy before flap elevation
answerChoices.rationale: The valid deeper measurement supports nodal-staging consideration despite a reassuring clinical basin; coordinating sentinel staging before flap reconstruction preserves mapping options.

answerChoices.label: Defer sentinel biopsy until after flap closure
answerChoices.rationale: A planned flap should not be completed ahead of the coordinated sentinel step simply because the local excision is finished.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A planned flap should not be completed ahead of the coordinated sentinel step simply because the local excision is finished.

answerChoices.label: Ultrasound surveillance after flap reconstruction
answerChoices.rationale: A smaller peripheral fragment and reassuring node morphology do not erase the valid deeper invasive measurement or replace microscopic staging.
answerChoices.distractorRationale: A smaller peripheral fragment and reassuring node morphology do not erase the valid deeper invasive measurement or replace microscopic staging.

question.explanation: The smaller peripheral fragment does not erase valid deeper invasion demonstrated centrally. Reassuring ultrasound is not microscopic nodal staging. With sentinel mapping already coordinated, complete the sentinel-node step before flap tissue rearrangement can interfere with later mapping. The constructed depths lie within the separately supported greater-than-1-mm discussion range; no new cutoff is introduced.

question.stem: Which regional-node assessment should be discussed with {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Sentinel lymph node mapping and biopsy

question.stem: Which diagnostic sampling plan should be used for {patientName}'s skin lesion?

answerChoices.label: Elliptical sampling of the lesion through the dermis into subcutaneous fat
answerChoices.rationale: Captures the heterogeneous lesion and a depth adequate for microstaging without committing to definitive wide margins before diagnosis.

answerChoices.label: Punch sampling of the darkest focus through the dermis into subcutaneous fat
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Can provide depth but risks selecting an unrepresentative component of a small heterogeneous lesion that can be sampled in its entirety.

answerChoices.label: Tangential sampling of the lesion across its surface and papillary dermis
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Captures surface extent but risks inadequate depth; this specific shallow plan is not a claim that every saucerization technique is inappropriate.

question.stem: Which diagnostic sampling plan should be used for {patientName}'s skin lesion?

answerChoices.label: Punch sampling of the darkest focus through the dermis into subcutaneous fat
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Can provide depth but risks selecting an unrepresentative component of a small heterogeneous lesion that can be sampled in its entirety.

answerChoices.label: Tangential sampling of the lesion across its surface and papillary dermis
answerChoices.distractorRationale: Captures surface extent but risks inadequate depth; this specific shallow plan is not a claim that every saucerization technique is inappropriate.

A targeted incisional sample is a real alternative when complete removal is impractical, but further levels of an existing block cannot create tissue that was never submitted.

Nivolumab is an approved adjuvant option for resected stage IIB/C melanoma. BRAF positivity does not transfer every stage III targeted-therapy indication into stage II.

authorGate.cueAttack: No stage label or 'immunotherapy eligible' conclusion is supplied. Drug names have comparable specificity; BRAF mutation intentionally makes the targeted pair tempting rather than uniquely matching the key.
authorGate.decisionStage: Systemic adjuvant drug options after definitive local and sentinel treatment.
reasoningSteps: Combine thickness, ulceration and node negativity to identify the relevant high-risk localized stage.
Separate anti-PD-1 stage II eligibility from the node-positive evidence boundary for BRAF-targeted adjuvant therapy.
authorGate.closestError: Let a BRAF mutation override the stage-specific indication.
authorGate.decidingObservation: Ulcerated 3.4-mm primary with negative sentinel nodes, rather than resected regional-node involvement.
authorGate.consequence: The wrong stage-to-regimen mapping can miss an evidence-based referral or propose an unsupported adjuvant indication.
authorGate.deletionTest: Removing ulceration or nodal status destroys the adjuvant boundary; removing BRAF removes the closest credible error. Recovery/immunosuppression context prevents a hidden treatment-phase contradiction.
authorGate.counterfactual: If regional nodes contained melanoma after complete resection, dabrafenib-trametinib would become a legitimate competing adjuvant option and this single-key set would need revision.
authorGate.difficultyReason: Requires stage-sensitive treatment reasoning despite a salient actionable mutation and another actual melanoma immunotherapy.
authorGate.sequenceReview: Standalone. No prior node calls the patient stage IIB or names anti-PD-1 therapy.
authorGate.repairAndRecheck: Replaced historical interferon with a real alternative melanoma checkpoint drug and kept the task about a phase-specific option for discussion, not universal treatment preference.

choices.rationale: The BRAF result is relevant, but established adjuvant use of this pair concerns resected node-positive disease rather than this node-negative stage II primary.
choices.counterfactual: Resected BRAF V600-mutant melanoma with regional node involvement would make this a real adjuvant option.

choices.rationale: Its established adjuvant evidence concerns high-risk resected regional disease; it is not the selected stage IIB/C anti-PD-1 option.
choices.counterfactual: Completely resected stage III melanoma is the setting of the established ipilimumab adjuvant evidence, although modern alternatives and toxicity still matter.

choices.rationale: Completed local therapy, ulcerated intermediate-thickness primary and negative sentinel staging fit a high-risk node-negative adjuvant anti-PD-1 discussion.
choices.counterfactual: A low-risk stage IA primary would not support the same routine adjuvant discussion.

authorGate.cueAttack: The update provides actual longitudinal observations without announcing drug failure. Each option names a specific same-cancer systemic strategy; the new drug name is not uniquely qualified.
authorGate.decisionStage: Next systemic treatment after a documented response followed by progression.
reasoningSteps: Interpret enlarging disease and new matched metastatic tissue as current progression despite earlier response.
Apply the post-Hedgehog indication to the next systemic treatment discussion.
authorGate.closestError: Keep crediting the initial response or assume switching within the Hedgehog class resolves progression.
authorGate.decidingObservation: New biopsy-confirmed deposits and serial enlargement during continued vismodegib.
authorGate.consequence: A historical-response shortcut can delay reassessment of an ineffective course.
authorGate.deletionTest: Without the later progression record, continued vismodegib is plausible; host context prevents a hidden immunotherapy exclusion.
authorGate.counterfactual: Sustained tumor control without new deposits would make continuing vismodegib the appropriate offered option.
authorGate.difficultyReason: Requires judging the current trajectory rather than the initial response, then applying the prior-drug-class boundary.
authorGate.sequenceReview: Standalone because the proposed earlier systemic-choice feedback rehearsed this later indication. Separating the cases removes that answer-specific prior scaffold; all necessary treatment history remains in the current record.
authorGate.repairAndRecheck: Split the proposed two-node course after the sequence cue attack. Re-solved the independent record using current observed progression; no universal cross-resistance rule or exact time to progression is asserted.

choices.rationale: The early response does not negate subsequent documented progression during ongoing treatment.
choices.counterfactual: Continuing an effective tolerated course would be reasonable if current examinations showed sustained control rather than progression.

choices.rationale: Another inhibitor in the same pathway is not established here as the preferred strategy for progression during vismodegib.
choices.counterfactual: An appropriate advanced local BCC patient who had not developed class-treatment resistance could be considered for an available Hedgehog inhibitor; this is not a universal post-progression interchangeability rule.

choices.rationale: Progression after Hedgehog therapy establishes the relevant later BCC indication for checkpoint evaluation.
choices.counterfactual: A major immune contraindication would require another specialist plan rather than assuming this option is safe.

decision.title: Choose a representative diagnostic specimen from the map

cues.phrase: the fragment diagnosis is not relabelled
cues.why: This unnecessary caption tells the learner to retain the benign fragment diagnosis rather than reconsider it. It weakly coaches evidence interpretation, but does not choose between complete excision and a targeted deep punch; both respect that diagnosis.

fairness: Original flag resolved: YES at the objective level for the mapped importance concern; no separate in-game flag is recorded. Owner b1-B12-context note fully resolved: YES. Choosing a representative next diagnostic specimen for an interval-changing residual lesion is a practical decision, rather than debating a report/request label.

Moderate at the lower end for PGY-2/3. First recognize that the valid benign lateral fragment does not establish the nature of the new unsampled medial focus; then choose complete diagnostic sampling over a second focal sample or observation. The targeted medial deep punch is a materially closer competitor than the prior wrong-block or superficial-biopsy foils.

Narrow-margin excision is the best offered diagnostic approach for the described small discrete residual upper-arm patch. The specimen map and interval change establish why the existing benign sample cannot settle the whole-lesion question. A side-edge melanocytic proliferation alone should not be taught as an automatic malignancy or excision indication.

A deep targeted punch is not inherently invalid and can be appropriate when complete sampling is unsuitable. The supplied small discrete patch and ordinary upper-arm site support the ranking here without the prohibited closure-feasibility assurance. The review does not infer an exact lesion diameter, closure technique or universal excision rule.

No equally strong offered key or confident clinical inaccuracy identified in this particular setting. 'Narrow-margin' should remain a diagnostic procedure, not an implied definitive melanoma excision or invented margin width. Clinician confirmation of the intended depth/completeness remains necessary.

The former classic-color and closure-permission cues are removed. Both biopsy options address the newly described medial area, and two options repeat 'residual patch', so simple location/phrase matching does not uniquely select the key.
suggestions: Trim the caption to 'Specimen and interval record'; the fragment-diagnosis commentary is unnecessary even though it does not reveal the complete key.

Retain the mapped sample location, interval change and credible targeted-biopsy alternative. Keep the explanation explicit that the old fragment may be correctly diagnosed while the residual lesion is not fully assessed.
Have clinical sign-off confirm that the excision label communicates complete diagnostic sampling at appropriate depth without adding an unsupported numerical margin or a feasibility sentence.

choices.rationale: Completion dissection can improve regional control but is not routinely required for a microscopic positive sentinel node with feasible ultrasound surveillance.
choices.counterfactual: Gross persistent regional disease or inability to deliver surveillance could change the regional-control discussion.

choices.rationale: The microscopic finding and available surveillance support avoiding routine completion dissection while oncology review continues.
choices.counterfactual: A growing biopsy-proven residual basin mass would require reassessment rather than the same observation pathway.

choices.rationale: Routine nodal irradiation is not established as the default response to this isolated microscopic SLN finding.
choices.counterfactual: Selected high-risk regional recurrence after therapeutic nodal treatment can prompt a radiation discussion.

choices.rationale: The BRAF result is relevant, but established adjuvant use of this pair concerns resected node-positive disease rather than this node-negative stage II primary.
choices.counterfactual: Resected BRAF V600-mutant melanoma with regional node involvement would make this a real adjuvant option.

choices.rationale: Its established adjuvant evidence concerns high-risk resected regional disease; it is not the selected stage IIB/C anti-PD-1 option.
choices.counterfactual: Completely resected stage III melanoma is the setting of the established ipilimumab adjuvant evidence, although modern alternatives and toxicity still matter.

choices.rationale: Completed local therapy, ulcerated intermediate-thickness primary and negative sentinel staging fit a high-risk node-negative adjuvant anti-PD-1 discussion.
choices.counterfactual: A low-risk stage IA primary would not support the same routine adjuvant discussion.

choices.rationale: The early response does not negate subsequent documented progression during ongoing treatment.
choices.counterfactual: Continuing an effective tolerated course would be reasonable if current examinations showed sustained control rather than progression.

choices.rationale: Another inhibitor in the same pathway is not established here as the preferred strategy for progression during vismodegib.

choices.rationale: Progression after Hedgehog therapy establishes the relevant later BCC indication for checkpoint evaluation.
choices.counterfactual: A major immune contraindication would require another specialist plan rather than assuming this option is safe.

choices.rationale: This would sample both appearances but still leave part of a small, readily excisable heterogeneous lesion unassessed.
choices.counterfactual: A much larger lesion whose complete diagnostic removal would require major reconstruction could justify a representative incisional sample.

choices.rationale: The local benign punch result does not characterize the entire patch; complete diagnostic architecture and depth can be obtained without a major repair.
choices.counterfactual: If the concerning lesion had already been completely assessed and no residual abnormality remained, another diagnostic excision would not automatically be indicated.

choices.rationale: Targeting the most concerning focus improves on the first sample, but a second fragment can still miss heterogeneity when complete removal is feasible.
choices.counterfactual: A broad lesion at a constrained site could justify a carefully selected full-depth partial biopsy.

choices.rationale: This uses the thinner residual focus as though it replaced the reliable 2.6-mm measurement from the same primary.
choices.counterfactual: If the greatest reliably measured invasive thickness across both specimens were 0.6 mm, a 1-cm margin would be appropriate.

choices.rationale: Retain the greater reliable invasive thickness, 2.6 mm, when planning the primary's definitive margin.

choices.rationale: The in-situ component in the later report does not erase the documented invasive primary.

singleSourceLimitations.limitation: Single directly checked government source for the biopsy preference; specimen-map applications are reasoned applications, not an exact biopsy-size rule. Deep saucerization is not declared universally inappropriate.
No new microstaging formula or protected AJCC table is reproduced. All patient measurements are constructed observations.
Single directly checked surgical guideline; complete histologic clearance remains necessary and lentigo maligna may require a different strategy. This is not a universal adequate final margin.
Single directly checked government summary of randomized evidence; no exact rate or individual prediction is taught.
Single current government evidence synthesis; BRAF mutation does not erase stage-specific eligibility. The draft asks which option merits discussion, not that one anti-PD-1 agent is superior.
Single adequate current source. Comparative choice among anti-PD-1 monotherapy and combinations is not scored; contraindications still require specialist assessment.
Single current government evidence synthesis; cytotoxic treatment remains a palliative option in selected patients. No regimen dose or comparative survival percentage is asserted.
Used to distinguish actual melanoma agents by evidence setting; substantial toxicity and modern alternatives prevent a universal preference claim.
No first-line ranking in BRAF-mutant metastatic disease, exact regimen or resistance timeline is asserted.
Single directly checked guideline; punch, shave and excisional techniques can each be appropriate. The examples do not claim one universal technique.
Single directly checked guideline; applies to conventional excision and significant rearrangement. No universal margin width or waiting duration is inferred.
Single government source. Reconstruction extent, morbidity and nonsurgical alternatives need individualized clinical review; no fixed re-excision margin is inferred.
Single government synthesis; no claim that every advanced BCC must receive this drug or that another Hedgehog inhibitor is universally equivalent after progression.
Single adequate current government drug-indication source; comparative sequencing evidence is limited, and no immunotherapy toxicity management regimen is taught.
Single directly checked current guideline; prior diagnostic biopsy is not an automatic contraindication. Post-rearrangement false-negative concerns are not treated as a universally invalid test.
Single directly checked current guideline; survival benefit and optimal cytotoxic regimen remain uncertain. This does not make it the default initial strategy for an eligible patient.

evidenceClaims.statement: Complete diagnostic sampling is preferred for a small accessible lesion suspicious for melanoma before definitive margin planning.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked government source for the biopsy preference; specimen-map applications are reasoned applications, not an exact biopsy-size rule. Deep saucerization is not declared universally inappropriate.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: A result from a mapped fragment does not establish the histology or maximum invasive depth of tissue outside that fragment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Scope/adequacy synthesis; retain valid local findings. These sources do not supply a universal rebiopsy interval or an automatic rule that every partial biopsy is inadequate.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Breslow thickness is a vertical histologic measurement used in primary melanoma treatment planning.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No new microstaging formula or protected AJCC table is reproduced. All patient measurements are constructed observations.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: A cutaneous melanoma on the trunk or extremity thicker than 2 mm generally requires a 2-cm clinical radial excision margin.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Not a universal rule for 1-2-mm lesions, facial lentigo maligna or anatomically constrained sites; diagnostic clearance does not replace therapeutic margins.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: A completely assessed invasive cutaneous melanoma no thicker than 1 mm can generally be treated with a 1-cm clinical radial margin.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Used for a distractor's decision-changing counterfactual, not to determine a margin from a transected or unrepresentative specimen.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: A 0.5-cm initial clinical radial margin is among accepted excision approaches for fully assessed melanoma in situ.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked surgical guideline; complete histologic clearance remains necessary and lentigo maligna may require a different strategy. This is not a universal adequate final margin.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Ulceration can support discussing sentinel-node staging for a clinically node-negative melanoma thinner than 0.8 mm.
evidenceClaims.limitation: A discussion, not a mandatory procedure or quantified risk. Pathologic ulceration must be distinguished from a traumatic surface defect; thin-melanoma guidance varies.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: For an appropriate clinically node-negative melanoma candidate, sentinel-node mapping is ideally coordinated with wide excision before major reconstructive rearrangement.
evidenceClaims.limitation: A prior narrow diagnostic excision is not equated with a prior wide excision and rotation flap. No claim that all later mapping invariably fails.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Microscopic sentinel-node melanoma can be managed with close nodal ultrasound observation instead of routine completion dissection when surveillance is feasible.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Selected positive-SLN setting, not bulky clinically apparent nodal disease or inability to attend surveillance. Regional control and melanoma-specific survival are different outcomes.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Trials of routine completion dissection after a positive melanoma sentinel node did not demonstrate a melanoma-specific survival advantage over nodal observation with ultrasound.
evidenceClaims.limitation: This is a trial-population finding, not proof of equivalence in every burden or follow-up setting. Regional-control outcomes differ.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Completion dissection after a positive melanoma sentinel node caused more lymphedema than ultrasound-based nodal observation in the randomized comparison.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked government summary of randomized evidence; no exact rate or individual prediction is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Completely resected stage IIB/C melanoma can prompt oncology discussion of adjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy despite a negative sentinel node.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No assertion that every eligible patient should receive nivolumab or that recurrence-free benefit proves an overall-survival advantage. Exact regimen is not taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: The established adjuvant dabrafenib-trametinib evidence concerns resected BRAF V600-mutant melanoma with regional node involvement, not every BRAF-mutant stage II primary.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current government evidence synthesis; BRAF mutation does not erase stage-specific eligibility. The draft asks which option merits discussion, not that one anti-PD-1 agent is superior.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Checkpoint immunotherapy is a systemic option for unresectable metastatic cutaneous melanoma regardless of BRAF mutation status.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate current source. Comparative choice among anti-PD-1 monotherapy and combinations is not scored; contraindications still require specialist assessment.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: In immunotherapy-eligible advanced melanoma, anti-PD-1 treatment has improved outcomes compared with routine initial cytotoxic chemotherapy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single current government evidence synthesis; cytotoxic treatment remains a palliative option in selected patients. No regimen dose or comparative survival percentage is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Established adjuvant ipilimumab evidence concerns completely resected high-risk regional melanoma rather than a universal stage II indication.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Used to distinguish actual melanoma agents by evidence setting; substantial toxicity and modern alternatives prevent a universal preference claim.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy for advanced melanoma requires an actionable BRAF V600 alteration; BRAF-wild-type disease is not selected for that treatment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No first-line ranking in BRAF-mutant metastatic disease, exact regimen or resistance timeline is asserted.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Biopsy for suspected cSCC must provide enough representative tissue for diagnosis and risk assessment, with repeat sampling when the first specimen is inadequate.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline; punch, shave and excisional techniques can each be appropriate. The examples do not claim one universal technique.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Poor differentiation, perineural invasion and recurrence can change cSCC risk-directed local treatment despite a small surface diameter.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No complete prognostic staging system, risk percentage or small-nerve radiation threshold is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: High-risk localized cSCC merits a margin-controlled surgical pathway such as Mohs rather than destructive treatment.
evidenceClaims.limitation: This does not resolve Mohs versus fully specified staged conventional excision. That exact owner hold persists.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: When high-risk cSCC is treated by conventional excision, major tissue rearrangement should await confirmation of clear histologic margins.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline; applies to conventional excision and significant rearrangement. No universal margin width or waiting duration is inferred.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Standard excision with a 4- to 6-mm clinical margin and histologic assessment is recommended for a properly assessed low-risk primary cSCC.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No claim of universal superiority over every other local modality. The exact 4-mm option is within the guideline's directly supported range; high-risk margins are not universalized.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Larger or less differentiated cSCC can require wider individualized excision margins than a low-risk primary.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Used only for a distractor counterfactual; NCI describes 6- to 10-mm margins in selected larger, less differentiated or high-risk-site tumors. No universal high-risk width is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Adults with high-risk cSCC after surgery and radiation may be evaluated for adjuvant cemiplimab under the October 2025 FDA indication.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Regulatory notice plus government drug-summary cross-check, not two independent trials. Solid-organ transplant recipients were excluded from C-POST and are not generalized into this key.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Histologically recurrent facial BCC is an indication for Mohs micrographic surgery.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Specific recurrent facial setting. No universal superiority claim for every small primary BCC or comparison against expertly staged equivalent margin control.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Topical imiquimod is an option for selected superficial low-risk BCC rather than a substitute for margin-controlled treatment of recurrent infiltrative facial disease.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Selection depends on histology, site and patient factors; no dose, duration or universal comparison with surgery is authored.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Residual BCC at a surgical margin can require further excision even when no tumor is visible at the healing site.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single government source. Reconstruction extent, morbidity and nonsurgical alternatives need individualized clinical review; no fixed re-excision margin is inferred.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Vismodegib is a systemic option for advanced BCC when curative local treatment is unsuitable.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single government synthesis; no claim that every advanced BCC must receive this drug or that another Hedgehog inhibitor is universally equivalent after progression.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Advanced BCC that progresses after Hedgehog-pathway treatment can be evaluated for cemiplimab.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single adequate current government drug-indication source; comparative sequencing evidence is limited, and no immunotherapy toxicity management regimen is taught.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: MCC diagnosis uses the morphology and combined epithelial/neuroendocrine panel; CK20 or TTF1 is not an absolute stand-alone diagnostic rule.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Uncommon staining exceptions persist. The frozen A28 approved version is preserved; the new questions do not require a hidden stain result.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Normal examination and negative imaging do not exclude microscopic regional MCC; a fit clinically node-negative patient should be considered for sentinel-node staging.
evidenceClaims.limitation: No exact positivity rate is taught, and negative imaging is not misrepresented as absence of staging value.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: MCC sentinel-node staging should be coordinated with local surgery before wide excision disrupts drainage.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked current guideline; prior diagnostic biopsy is not an automatic contraindication. Post-rearrangement false-negative concerns are not treated as a universally invalid test.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: For most immunotherapy-eligible patients with unresectable or metastatic MCC, PD-1/PD-L1 therapy is preferred over routine initial cytotoxic chemotherapy.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Predominantly nonrandomized evidence. Do not choose among equally supported checkpoint agents or generalize to transplant recipients.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

evidenceClaims.statement: Platinum-etoposide is a real advanced-MCC chemotherapy option when immunotherapy is contraindicated or has failed.
evidenceClaims.limitation: Single directly checked current guideline; survival benefit and optimal cytotoxic regimen remain uncertain. This does not make it the default initial strategy for an eligible patient.
evidenceClaims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the exact synthetic clinic/chart-review scenarios; exclusions and care phase are item-specific.

cues.phrase: A firm base remains at that same site
cues.why: Only 'Full-thickness incisional biopsy through the firm base' repeats the exact target. Both distractors evade it.

fairness: The explanation correctly distinguishes evidence for an in-situ component from proof that the unsampled base lacks invasion. Full-thickness representative sampling is a defensible offered next step.
The task has already decided that more tissue is needed before treatment. With both alternatives confined to epidermis, the apparent second decision is removed.
The later node uses a complete diagnostic excision rather than the selected incisional biopsy; this transition needs explanation in that follow-up.
suggestions: Keep the essential absence of evaluable underlying dermis; do not hide that limitation to manufacture difficulty.
Rebuild the comparison around plausible diagnostic strategies that all address the relevant site, with specimen depth/extent and real procedure constraints deciding between them.
Avoid having the task preselect additional sampling if the intended inference is whether the existing report can support definitive treatment.

originalReview.title: Standard-excision margin after low-risk invasive cSCC is established
clarityIssues: The previous keyed action was full-thickness incisional biopsy. 'A later complete diagnostic excision' introduces another procedure without explaining the intervening course.
'Complete diagnostic excision' alongside tumor at a side edge can be read as contradictory unless complete refers to gross lesion removal rather than histologic clearance.

cues.phrase: Standard excision with a 4-mm radial margin
cues.why: Only 4 mm is a modest margin; the two much larger alternatives create weak competition for a tiny lesion with an explicitly favorable risk profile. This is a clinical plausibility weakness rather than a deterministic numerical or wording cue.

fairness: The location, size, differentiation, depth, primary status and host context support a low-risk interpretation, followed by selecting a standard margin. The stated 4-mm answer is within the explanation's 4-6-mm range; it is not uniquely required over every unlisted value in that range.
All choices already require excision, so the involved side edge does not independently test whether clearance is necessary.
The follow-up otherwise stands alone using its own complete pathology. Earlier feedback does not disclose the numerical margin. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline.
suggestions: Clarify the interval procedure and distinguish grossly complete removal from histologic margin clearance.

Replace the exaggerated widths with credible errors such as diagnostic versus definitive extent, while avoiding multiple options within the accepted range. A range-based answer may represent the teaching point more faithfully.
Preserve risk-defining facts; do not add or invent high-risk cutoffs merely to make the item harder.

originalReview.title: Reconstruction timing after high-risk ear cSCC excision
clarityIssues: 'Shave the wound bed' does not say whether tissue is sent for analysis, how it is oriented or whether a result is available before closure. It is too underspecified to be a credible margin-assessment plan.

cues.phrase: its permanent-section margin report will be returned after the procedure
cues.why: This is necessary chronology, but the options turn it into a direct before/after match: only the key explicitly waits for clearance.

cues.phrase: Dress the defect and repair after clear permanent margins
cues.why: Only the key names a verified endpoint. The other two choices both complete the flap without any stated result, making the key the uniquely cautious plan.

fairness: Delaying significant tissue rearrangement until clearance is established is a defensible plan for this recurrent, poorly differentiated cSCC under the stipulated conventional-excision pathway.
The meaningful risk classification does little work because the option set already advertises one checked plan and two unchecked plans. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline.
suggestions: Specify the wound-bed alternative's actual assessment method and timing rather than leaving its mechanism undefined.

Compare concrete reconstructive/margin workflows with comparable detail and genuine tradeoffs. Require interpretation of an actual margin map or report rather than merely choosing the only option that says 'clear'.

originalReview.title: Adjuvant cemiplimab after resection and radiation for high-risk cSCC
clarityIssues: The explanation's 'owner/oncologist' addresses the authoring workflow rather than the resident's clinical decision.

cues.phrase: Cemiplimab
cues.why: The competitors are drugs associated with other skin-cancer pathways, so the item reduces to matching a named cancer to its drug. This requires drug knowledge, but none of the detailed postoperative risk information is needed to distinguish these options.

fairness: No confident clinical inaccuracy is asserted. The claimed recent adjuvant indication and its precise high-risk eligibility are not independently verified in this offline review; extranodal extension alone should not silently substitute for any additional criteria a specific trial or label may require.
The task presupposes that a systemic adjuvant treatment merits evaluation. It therefore does not test the important decision about adjuvant care despite no visible residual disease.

This is a useful evolving oncology topic, but the exact recent indication is not established here as a commonly tested general-surgery concept; highYield=false reflects that limited exam-relevance judgment, not clinical unimportance.
suggestions: Have the clinician verify the exact current indication and supply any decision-critical eligibility findings using permitted evidence; do not invent nodal thresholds.
Reframe around whether the documented postoperative risk justifies a specific adjuvant discussion, using credible same-disease plans rather than unrelated targeted agents.
Remove 'owner' from learner feedback and clearly distinguish consideration from automatic treatment.

originalReview.title: Local treatment of recurrent infiltrative nasal BCC
clarityIssues: The standard-excision option leaves its margin-assessment workflow unspecified, yet immediate repair is treated as the decisive defect.

cues.phrase: Mohs excision followed by margin-cleared repair
cues.why: Only the key explicitly promises clearance, while its surgical rival emphasizes immediate repair. This repeats the uniquely checked-plan structure seen in the cSCC item.

cues.phrase: Topical imiquimod treatment of the scar
cues.why: It is a weak competitor for biopsy-confirmed recurrent infiltrative nasal disease; 'scar' also downplays the documented nodule and infiltrative border.

fairness: The scar-site history, infiltrative histology and indistinct border support interpreting this as high-risk disease despite small visible size. Mohs is a defensible best offered treatment.
Do not teach that every standard excision followed by immediate repair is invalid without specifying its clearance method. The closest surgical competitor needs enough detail to assess fairly.
'This is a procedure decision rather than another pearly nodule label question' is editorial commentary in learner feedback, not a useful explanation of management.
suggestions: Make both surgical options equally explicit about margin assessment and repair timing; support the deciding difference with the actual case.
Replace the weak topical foil with a credible management error for recurrent disease, avoiding an equally acceptable margin-controlled alternative as a false distractor.
Delete the explanation's editorial comparison to other questions and teach why visible diameter underestimates the relevant extent.

originalReview.title: Positive BCC deep margin before planned scar revision
clarityIssues: 'Scar revision through the healed incision' is vague about what tissue is removed and whether histology is obtained. It may overlap with field re-excision unless its scope is defined.

A healed wound with contracture is plausible, but the interval from excision to this visit is unstated; the sequence should not suggest that an involved margin was knowingly ignored without explanation.

cues.phrase: infiltrative tumor at the deep inked edge
cues.why: Only the key treats an involved field and includes margin assessment; the surface-sampling distractor advertises a depth mismatch.

cues.phrase: Superficial punch sampling of the scar surface
cues.why: The redundant superficial/surface wording announces inadequacy after a deep-edge finding, rather than describing a realistic competing procedure.

fairness: Histologic involvement warrants addressing local clearance despite a normal-looking healed site; re-excision with margin assessment is defensible.
The alternatives do not create a genuine two-step decision: one is undefined cosmetic surgery and one explicitly examines the wrong depth. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline.
suggestions: Define the intended scope of scar revision so it cannot encompass oncologic re-excision.
Use a credible competing clearance strategy or an interpretable specimen-orientation problem, with enough findings to make one approach best. Remove the intentionally superficial caricature.
Clarify the relevant interval or outside-record chronology without adding an invented treatment deadline.

originalReview.title: Initial systemic therapy for advanced BCC

cues.phrase: has no contraindication to a Hedgehog-pathway inhibitor
cues.why: The stem names the keyed therapeutic class and supplies its eligibility conclusion. A learner who recognizes drug classes can answer without deriving the treatment sequence.

cues.phrase: Carboplatin plus etoposide
cues.why: This is a different cutaneous-cancer treatment association rather than a strong initial advanced-BCC competitor; it leaves a largely class-name matching exercise.

fairness: Vismodegib is a defensible initial option under the stated local-treatment limitations and Hedgehog suitability; cemiplimab is the meaningful sequencing distractor.
The multidisciplinary conclusion can legitimately establish that curative local treatments are unsuitable. The added class-specific permission, however, announces the remaining inference.

The exact systemic sequencing objective is narrower and less clearly commonly tested than BCC diagnosis/local clearance. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline; current indication boundaries still require clinician confirmation.
suggestions: Replace the Hedgehog-class permission with only the actual decision-critical history or findings needed to resolve eligibility; do not omit necessary contraindication information.
Require a consequential interpretation of prior treatment or a concrete eligibility issue before choosing among credible advanced-BCC plans.
If retained as basic pharmacology recognition, label and accept that role explicitly instead of claiming two-step resident difficulty.

originalReview.title: Systemic treatment after BCC progression on vismodegib
fairness: The learner must distinguish the initial response from current progression on continued therapy, then use the prior drug class to select a different indicated pathway. Continuing the initially effective agent and switching within the Hedgehog class are recognizable competing errors.
Biopsy-confirmed new liver deposits and serial enlargement make the present response unambiguous. The history needed to consider checkpoint treatment is supplied without naming that class in advance.

Cemiplimab is the defensible offered next evaluation; no confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline. This review does not imply every same-class switch is impossible in every different clinical setting.
This is a separate patient and case from the initial-Hedgehog item, not its later node. The stem stands alone, though prior bank exposure to that other item's feedback would reduce novelty.

Useful advanced-treatment coverage, but the exact post-Hedgehog sequence is a narrower oncology gap than a clearly common general-surgery board concept; highYield=false does not mean clinically unimportant.
suggestions: No required scoring repair. Optionally remove the final feedback sentence about what is 'asserted' and teach the progression-versus-intolerance distinction directly; the current final sentence is editorial clutter rather than a key error.
Retain this as a specialist gap item rather than using its drug-sequence difficulty to represent the core surgical topic.

originalReview.title: Nodal staging of Merkel carcinoma despite negative PET/CT

cues.phrase: Which regional staging plan should accompany {patientName}'s planned forearm excision?
cues.why: Only the key says 'with local excision'; both distractors say 'after local excision'. The lead-in favors the key's timing before the learner considers microscopic disease.

cues.phrase: Repeat PET/CT after local excision
cues.why: The scan has just been described as negative with no intervening change. Repeating the same completed comparison is a weak foil beside the only new tissue-based staging plan.

fairness: Negative examination and PET/CT do not establish absence of microscopic nodal disease; sentinel mapping/biopsy coordinated with primary surgery is a defensible key.
The necessary negative imaging should remain. The problem is a single familiar staging rule combined with options whose timing and novelty announce the answer, not an inaccurate clinical premise.
The later metastatic update is clearly labeled later and does not contaminate this node. This explanation does not reveal the later systemic drug answer.
suggestions: Use a neutral complete task such as asking which regional staging plan is appropriate now, without 'accompany'.

Balance the timing and novelty of alternatives and introduce a supported staging/operative-sequence distinction that requires interpreting the actual record. Do not remove negative PET findings or pretend they prove microscopic clearance.

originalReview.title: Initial systemic treatment of metastatic Merkel carcinoma

cues.phrase: multiple biopsy-confirmed MCC deposits in both lungs and liver. These cannot all be removed
cues.why: The extent and systemic-treatment decision are already interpreted, and every option is a systemic drug. The distribution does not create an additional scored inference.

cues.phrase: Vismodegib
cues.why: This is a drug-disease mismatch foil, leaving checkpoint therapy versus a historical chemotherapy regimen rather than two consequential decisions.

fairness: Pembrolizumab is a defensible initial systemic discussion for this eligible advanced-MCC patient; the explanation appropriately avoids claiming unique superiority over other checkpoint agents.

The earlier negative PET/CT and current metastases are not contradictory because the update explicitly describes later records after local treatment. The current update supplies sufficient disease and treatment history to stand alone, and earlier feedback does not name pembrolizumab.

This remains a first-line drug-selection rule. The exact drug choice in rare advanced MCC is less clearly a commonly tested general-surgery concept than MCC nodal staging; the broad checkpoint-treatment principle is clinically relevant. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified offline.
suggestions: Keep the clear interval chronology, but remove resolved history that does not change the systemic comparison.

Develop a supported clinical sequencing or eligibility conflict with credible same-disease alternatives, or explicitly accept a foundational drug-selection role. Do not make difficulty depend on substituting an equally acceptable checkpoint agent as a distractor.
